DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph on-G NO. IL FEB 0 3 2025 EUSTAQUIO V. ANGELES Operations Controller ARC Refreshments Corporation 3rd Floor Solmac Bldg., Banaue cor. Dapitan St., Quezon City Dear Mr. Angeles: This pertains to your Letter dated October 28, 2024, requesting this Department's legal opinion on whether Quezon City is entitled to the 30% allocation of sales generated from ARC Refreshments Corporation's branches located outside of Quezon City and that the corresponding business tax should be paid to Quezon City. Culled from your letter are the following pertinent factual antecedents: • • • ARC Refreshments Corporation (ARC) is a non-alcoholic beverage company with fifteen branches or sales offices operating nationwide. The Office of the City Treasurer in Quezon City (OTCT-QC) has issued a final demand letter on business taxes for the years 2017 to 2021 totaling to dated October 17, 2024. Per OTCT-QC assessment, ARC Head Office in Quezon City had underpaid business taxes due to the exclusion of the 30% share of the Head Office in the sales of its branches located outside of Quezon City that should be considered as the base for the computation of business tax. OTCT-QC contends that 30% of all ARC branches' sales should be included in the computation of business tax of its Head Office due to Quezon City, regardless of where the sales were generated. ARC operates branches outside of Quezon City that accept orders, issue their own sales invoices, and record sales transactions in the branch. These branches have their own business permits and BIR-registered sales invoices. Therefore, ARC records the sales in said branches or sales office and business tax paid to the city or municipality where the same is located. ARC operates the above-mentioned branches and sales offices that pay local business taxes to the cities or municipalities where the sales were generated. Hence, the subject query. At the outset, it bears noting that central to the issue at hand is the application of Section 150 of the Code, which establishes the "situs" or location where business taxes are due and payable, thus: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

"Section 150. Situs of the Tax. - (a) For purposes of collection of the taxes under Section 143 of this Code, manufacturers, assemblers, repackers, brewers, distillers, rectifiers and compounders of liquor, distilled spirits and wines, millers, producers, exporters, wholesalers, distributors, dealers, contractors, banks and other financial institutions, and other businesses, maintaining or operating branch or sales outlet elsewhere shall record the sale in the branch or sales outlet making the sale or transaction, and the tax thereon shall accrue and shall be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In cases where there is no such branch or sales outlet in the city or municipality where the sale or transaction is made, the sale shall be duly recorded in the principal office and the taxes due shall accrue and shall be paid to such city or municipality." (b) The following sales allocation shall apply to manufacturers, assemblers, contractors, producers, and exporters with factories, project offices, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business: (1) Thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the principal office is located, and (2) Seventy percent (70%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. (c) In case of a plantation located at a place other than the place where the factory is located, said seventy percent (70%) mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be divided as follows: (1) Sixty percent (60%) to the city or municipality where the factory is located; and (2) Forty percent (40%) to the city or municipality where the plantation is located. (d) In cases where a manufacturer, assembler, producer, exporter or contractor has two (2) or more factories, project offices, plants, or plantations located in different localities, the seventy percent (70%) sales allocation mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be prorated among the localities where the factories, project offices, plants, and plantations are located in proportion to their respective volumes of production during the period for which the tax is due. (e) The foregoing sales allocation shall be applied irrespective of whether or not sales are made in the locality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. (Emphasis ours) Corollarily, Article 243 of Administrative Order No. 270, Series of 1992, which prescribes for the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Code, is instructive, thus: "Article 243. Situs of the Tax. — (a) Definition of Terms — (a) Definition of Terms — Page 2 of 4

(1) Principal Office — the head or main office of the business appearing in the pertinent documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission, or the Department of Trade and Industry, or other appropriate agencies, as the case may be. The city or municipality specifically mentioned in the articles of incorporation of official registration papers as being the official address of said principal office shall be considered as the situs thereof. xxx (2) Branch or Sales Office — a fixed place in a locality which conducts operations of the business as an extension of the principal office. xxx (3) Project Office- shall mean the field office in the construction site. It is the equivalent to the factory of a manufacturer. (b) Sales Allocation — (1) All sales made in a locality where there is a branch or sales office or warehouse shall be recorded in said branch or sales office or warehouse and tax shall be payable to the city or municipality where the same is located. (2) In cases where there is no such branch, sales office, or warehouse in the locality where the sale is made, the sale shall be recoded in the principal office along with the sales made by said principal office and the tax shall accrue to the city or municipality where said principal office is located. (3) In cases where there is a factory, project office, plant or plantation in pursuit of business, thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the principal office is located and seventy (70%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office plant or plantation is located. LGUs where only experimental farms are located shall not entitled to the sales allocation provided in this subparagraph. xxx." (Emphasis ours) As can be deduced, paragraph a of Section 150 of the Code contemplates a case where a manufacturer (and those above-enumerated) maintains or operates a branch or sales outlet; the tax shall accrue and be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In the herein case, it bears noting that the operations of ARC's branches are distinct from its Principal or Head Office. As specifically represented, ARC operates branches outside of Quezon City that accept orders, issue their own sales invoices, and record sales transactions in the branch. Ostensibly, these branches have their own business permits and BIR-registered sales invoices. It is intimated that ARC records the sales in said branches or sales office and business tax paid to the city or municipality where the same is located. Accordingly, the sales generated by branches are subject to business tax in the city or municipality where they are located. Hence, following the situs principle as laid down in the above-quoted provision, OTCT- QC may not be entitled to the 30% allocation of sales generated from ARC's branches located outside of Quezon City; otherwise, it could constitute a double taxation. This Page 3 of4

Department opines that the OTCT-QC's contention that 30% of all branch sales should be included in the Principal Office tax base appears to be untenable. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 77, s. 2004, we opined that Section 150 (a) of the Code is rather explicit in stating that taxes due on branch sales shall accrue and be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In fine, it may not be amiss to note that the legislative intent behind the rule in situs of taxation—as enunciated in the Explanatory Note of a legislative measure seeking to strengthen local taxationl—is to guarantee that each LGU will receive its fair share of taxes from businesses operating within their respective jurisdictions. This opinion, however, shall be without prejudice to the position of the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) and the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) of the Department of Finance (DOF), as the same subject matter herein falls within the ambit of their administrative competence and expertise. In the same tone, please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: . ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jam Senate Bill 1320 "An Act Strengthening Local Taxation and the Fiscal Capacity of Local Government Units by Increasing their Tax Generation Capacity, Amending Section 150 of Republic Act No. 7160, Othemise Known as the 'Local Govemment Code Of 1991', and for Other Purposes", House of Representatives, 19th Congress.
